input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 is the only audit right binding us and it meets the preferred position in full: audits are limited to once in any twelve-month period, require thirty days' prior written notice, are during normal business hours, are conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and are at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds five percent (§ 22.2). Section 22.2 also expressly bars direct access to Customer systems, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material and third-party confidential information, so the walk-away risk (unannounced audits or remote system access) does not arise. Section 22.3 adds further customer protections (findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, shortfall payment resolves the issue). No redline needed.
